slides.say: A B C is an equilateral triangle. Point D lies on B C. Given: angle D A C is thirty degrees, and D C is seven centimeters. What is A B, in centimeters?
at: A B C is an equilateral

slides.say: A B is a side of the triangle, and in an equilateral triangle all the sides are equal. So we're really looking for the side. We know two things, the thirty degrees at A, and D C is seven. [short pause] We'll see what the line A D does in this triangle.

[short pause] A B C is equilateral, so all its angles are sixty. So the whole angle at A is sixty. Thirty of it is between A D and A C, so the other part, between A B and A D, is sixty minus thirty, which is thirty too.
at: So the whole angle at A

slides.say: So A D cuts the angle at A into two equal halves. It's the angle bisector. An equilateral triangle is symmetric from every direction, so this line from the top is also the altitude and the median. As a median, it cuts B C into two equal parts.
at: So A D cuts the angle

slides.say: So B D is seven too, and the whole side B C is seven plus seven, which is fourteen. All the sides are equal, so A B is fourteen. Choice number two is our answer.
at: So B D is seven too
Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Careful, seven, choice number one, is only half of the side. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
